resources.string: When BrailleBack is on, your device will connect to a paired bluetooth braille display and present the screen content in braille. Keys on the braille display can be used to navigate the screen, activate items and enter text. For more information, press space and dots 1, 2 and 3 (the letter l in braille) on your display when connected.
To use the braille hardware keyboard, you need to enable it in the input method settings and then set it as the default input method.
To use the braille hardware keyboard, you need to set it as the default input method.
Allows an app to write output to and and read keyboad input from a braille display

Connect automatically at startup, when the screen or Bluetooth turns on, or when a paired display is discovered; retry briefly after a drop and wait for the display to reconnect

The braille overlay simulates a refreshable braille display. It displays the braille cells, along with the corresponding text, that would be presented on a hardware display. It is recommended that you enable TalkBack and touch exploration mode before proceeding.
You can pan the braille display by pressing one of the panning buttons next to the text.

Multiple elements may appear on the display at once. You can click on one of them by tapping one of the braille cells in the text. This corresponds to pressing one of the routing keys on a braille display.

If the overlay is covering another element on the screen, you can move it out of the way. Long-press the overlay, and then drag it. It will snap to the top or bottom of the screen when you release your finger.
We recommend that you view the tutorial for the on-screen overlay before using it.
Search on screen allows you to quickly jump to items on the screen by typing part of their text description. As you type, focus will move to the next matching item.
Use %1$s to move to the next result and %2$s to move to the previous result. Press %3$s to exit the search mode and keep focus on the result. Press %4$s to move back to the previously focused item.

string-array.item: Settings - Apps - App management: find this braille app
Battery saver: set it to No restrictions
Recents: lock the card so clean-up does not kill it
Settings - Apps - App launch: turn off automatic management, allow autostart
Battery - More battery settings: allow background activity
Settings - Battery - App power management: allow background running
Settings - App management - Autostart: turn it on
Settings - Battery - High background power use: allow
iManager - App management - Autostart: turn it on
Settings - Battery - Background usage limits: add this app to Never sleeping apps
Device care: allow background activity for this app
